statement: Yes, webhooks are available on the Free plan — just add a Webhooks by Zapier trigger and you're set.

contexts.text: Webhooks by Zapier is a Premium app. It is available only on paid plans (Business tier and above). Free and Starter plans cannot use raw webhook triggers or actions.

statement: You can export all of your account data yourself from Settings > Data Export at any time.

contexts.text: There is no self-serve data export. Customers must file a request with the Trust team, who fulfil data exports manually within 30 days.

statement: Billing is monthly and you are charged only for the seats you use each month.

contexts.text: All plans are billed annually up front. Additional seats added mid-term are invoiced as a prorated true-up at renewal, not monthly.

statement: Task history is retained for 12 months on every plan.

contexts.text: Task history retention depends on plan: 7 days on Free, 30 days on Starter, and 3 months on Professional. Only Company plans retain task history for 12 months.

statement: Refunds are not possible once a subscription has started.

contexts.text: We offer a full refund within 30 days of the initial purchase or a plan upgrade, no questions asked.

statement: A Zap can have at most 5 steps.

contexts.text: Multi-step Zaps support up to 100 steps on paid plans. Free plans are limited to a single action step.

statement: Your documentation says custom logic filters run bottom to top, but support told me last month they run top to bottom.

contexts.text: Filters and paths in a Zap are evaluated in order from the top of the editor downward. The first matching path wins.

statement: SSO is included on the Team plan at no extra cost.

contexts.text: SAML SSO is an Enterprise-only feature and is not available on Team or Company plans.

statement: To get a webhook URL, add a 'Catch Hook' trigger and Zapier will generate a unique URL you can POST to.

contexts.text: The Webhooks by Zapier 'Catch Hook' trigger generates a unique URL. Send a POST request to that URL and Zapier will catch the payload and start the Zap.

statement: You can find your run logs on the Zap History page, filterable by Zap, date, and status.

contexts.text: Zap History shows every run of your Zaps. You can filter the list by Zap, by date range, and by status (success, error, filtered, held).

statement: API key auth is configured under the Authentication tab of your integration and sent as a header on each request.

contexts.text: In the Platform UI, choose 'API Key' on the Authentication tab. Define the key field and add it to the API Request as a header or query parameter that is included on every call.

statement: The 30-day retention on your plan means runs older than a month are removed from Zap History.

contexts.text: Starter plans retain task history for 30 days. After that window, individual run records are purged and no longer visible in Zap History.

statement: Because webhooks need a paid plan, you'd have to upgrade to Business before using a Catch Hook trigger.

contexts.text: Webhooks by Zapier is a Premium app available only on Business plans and above.

statement: Deduplication uses the 'id' field of each item, so reusing an id means the item is treated as already seen.

contexts.text: Polling triggers deduplicate on the item's 'id' field. If a new item reuses an id Zapier has seen before, it is considered a duplicate and does not trigger the Zap.

statement: Since data export isn't self-serve, I've opened a Trust-team request on your behalf and they'll deliver within 30 days.

contexts.text: Data exports are handled manually by the Trust team on request, with a 30-day SLA. There is no self-serve export option.

statement: Sub-accounts and shared app connections are a feature of the Company plan.

contexts.text: The Company plan adds shared app connections, sub-accounts, and advanced admin permissions on top of the Team plan.
